docs.summary:
Everything a [`SceneTool`](#api~Prowl.Editor.GUI.SceneView.SceneTool) needs for one viewport for one frame: the arbitration context, the scene, the selection, and per-viewport storage.

One context exists per scene viewport and is reused across frames, so [`State<T>`](#api~Prowl.Editor.GUI.SceneView.SceneToolContext~State) is stable for as long as the viewport lives. That is what lets a single tool instance serve two scene views without their drags interfering.
Handle arbitration, cursor, ray, camera and keyboard-safe key queries.
Deferred 3D drawing onto the viewport overlay.
The scene being edited in this viewport.
The camera used to render the viewport.
The viewport this context belongs to.
The first selected GameObject, or null if nothing is selected.
